subject: Model variant memory projections & pool rightsizing — HelioBio committed pool
messages:
From: Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@helio.bio>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing for long-context models (32k)/throughput target

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are close to locking in a committed reserved pool but need a grounded GPU sizing proposal tied to the model variants we plan to run. High-level details:
- Production models: two variants — "diagnostics-v1" (Llama-2 style 70B-ish, 32k context) and "assist-v2" (13B, 16k context)
- Expected steady-state: 25 concurrent inference sessions (interactive), average request length 600 tokens, average generation 150 tokens
- Peak bursts: up to 60 concurrent sessions for short windows
- SLA: p95 latency target ~350ms for assist-v2, ~600ms acceptable for diagnostics-v1 (long context)
- Interested in aggressive int8 quantization if it preserves quality; procurement may also prefer A100 vs H100 for cost reasons

Can you provide: an estimate of GPUs needed for the committed pool, how quantization impacts the per-GPU capacity for each variant, and recommended instance types (80GB vs 40GB) and mitigation if we need to support 32k KV cache growth?

Also looping in procurement at procurement@helio.bio for pricing cadence.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Sanders
Director, ML Platforms
HelioBio Inc.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@helio.bio>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for long-context models (32k)/throughput target

Hi Emma —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a first-pass projection (helio_memory_projections_v1.xlsx) and a rightsizing diagram. High-level summary up front:

1) Model memory & KV cache impact (per-GPU):
   - diagnostics-v1 (70B equivalent): baseline sharded model runtime memory ~40–48 GB on 16-bit execution; KV cache for 32k context adds ~20–26 GB of transient GPU memory when a session reaches max length.
   - assist-v2 (13B equivalent): baseline ~9–12 GB; 16k context KV cache adds ~4–6 GB.

2) Quantization impacts:
   - Int8 (dynamic) reduces model memory by ~28–35% on average in our tests — for diagnostics-v1 this drops the runtime model footprint by ~12–16 GB which materially reduces the need for 80GB-only GPUs.
   - Quality caveat: diagnostics-v1 shows small regression on some medical summarization prompts at aggressive int8; recommend running the eval suite you shared on the quantized build.

3) Suggested committed pool (steady-state + 2x burst headroom):
   - Conservative (no int8): 10 x 80GB GPUs (H100/A100 80GB) to meet p95 targets and headroom for bursts.
   - With int8 enabled on diagnostics-v1 and mixed precision for assist-v2: 7–8 x 80GB GPUs.
   - If you want to leverage cheaper 40GB GPUs (A100 40GB), you can tile—expect ~1.6x more GPUs and slightly higher latency variance.

4) Operational recommendations:
   - Canary quantized build for two weeks against production prompt set (we can run differential evals and regressions).
   - Set autoscale floor to the committed pool and keep a small burst credit for transient spikes.

Next steps I suggest: internal sizing check with engineering (quick call) and then we share the finalized numbers for procurement.

Cc'ing Lauren to validate the cluster tiling/tiling failover notes. Attaching the projection spreadsheet for line-item numbers.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for long-context models (32k)/throughput target

Looping Aditya for kernel/runtime validation. Quick notes from infra perspective:

- The per-session KV cache number Karthik shared looks reasonable as an upper bound if clients fully consume 32k. In practice we see a distribution where 80% of sessions stay below 8–12k; we should surface that distribution to Helio so they can consider a cheaper steady-state commit.
- For diagnostics-v1: if they commit to int8 but want deterministic p95, we should reserve some H100 80GB nodes for the canary/QA lane and route production traffic only after regression thresholds pass.
- Tiling across 40GB will work but increases threading and RPC overhead; estimate 15–20% latency uplift for p95 under load.

Aditya — can you confirm the numbers and add an expected tokens/sec per GPU row for both variants (fp16 vs int8)?

Thanks,
Lauren

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 14:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for long-context models (32k)/throughput target

Quick verification and numbers (we ran microbenchmarks similar to Helio's profile):

- diagnostics-v1 (70B class):
  - FP16 (no quant): sustained throughput per 80GB GPU for the workload described (avg request 600 + gen 150 tokens): ~7–9 interactive sessions with p95 around 450–700ms depending on placement and batch mixing.
  - INT8 dynamic: sessions per 80GB GPU rises to ~11–13 with a ~25–35% reduction in model memory footprint, leaving room for larger KV cache per GPU. Quality: small edge regressions; recommend rolling quantization behind feature flag.
  - KV cache growth: On GPU, KV memory scales ~linear with context. A 32k session requires ~22–26GB additional GPU memory over an 8k session in our runtime for this model class (includes key+value buffers across layers).

- assist-v2 (13B class):
  - FP16: ~18–22 sessions per 80GB GPU under the Helio profile; p95 ~220–300ms.
  - INT8: ~24–28 sessions per 80GB GPU. KV overhead at 16k is modest (~4–6GB).

Operational notes:
- For 25 steady interactive sessions with periodic bursts to 60, the 7–8 GPU estimate (with int8) assumes even distribution across GPUs and that only a fraction of sessions hit full 32k. If Helio expects many sessions to frequently consume full-context, push to 10 GPUs.
- If they choose 40GB GPUs: plan for ~12–15 A100-40GB equivalence with careful tiling; split diagnostics-v1 onto dedicated 80GB nodes to avoid tail latencies.

I'll add a small column in the spreadsheet with sessions-per-GPU and p95 estimates (fp16 vs int8).

—Aditya

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Sanders <emma.sanders@helio.bio>, procurement@helio.bio
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for long-context models (32k)/throughput target

Emma —

Thanks for the ask. Based on the runtime verification above and Helio's throughput targets, our recommended committed pool:

Option A (quality-first, no aggressive quantization):
- 10 x 80GB GPUs (H100/A100 80GB).
- This meets p95 targets with comfortable headroom for bursts and allows some sessions to hit full 32k without blocking.

Option B (cost-optimized, int8 enabled):
- 7 x 80GB GPUs with a 2-node (canary) lane reserved for regression checks.
- Expected to meet steady-state and p95 with caveat that we will run the quantized eval suite you provided.

If you'd like to reduce cost further by using 40GB hardware, we'd recommend mixing: dedicate 2–3 x 80GB nodes for diagnostics-v1 and run assist-v2 on tiled 40GBs. Note that tiled 40GB introduces ~15–20% p95 variance under mixed load.

I've attached the detailed spreadsheet and an initial mutual action plan in the Drive link. Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up Tuesday to lock on Option? Also confirm if procurement wants an itemized price cadence so I can push an MSA/quote.

Best,
Karthik
